sources.name: DataFixerUpper
sources.bestFor: Schema-driven serialized game data upgrades
sources.notes: Primary model for forward world and data migration. Downgrades need separate reversible transforms.

sources.name: Fabric API
sources.bestFor: Fabric events, registries, networking, rendering, resources, and GameTest helpers
sources.notes: Use source and changelog diffs to map API drift.

sources.name: Fabric automated testing
sources.bestFor: Fabric GameTest and automated launch testing
sources.notes: Core real-runtime verification layer for Fabric repairs.

sources.name: Fabric developer documentation
sources.bestFor: Fabric setup, Loom, networking, data generation, rendering, testing, and porting
sources.notes: Pair with Fabric API source and changelogs for exact removed symbols.

sources.name: Fabric Loader
sources.bestFor: Fabric mod discovery, metadata, dependency solving, remapping, and launch
sources.notes: Inspect loader internals only when metadata and public APIs are insufficient.

sources.name: Fabric Loom
sources.bestFor: Workspace setup, mappings, remapping, run configurations, access wideners, and publishing
sources.notes: Primary Fabric source reconstruction and remap tool.

sources.name: ForgeGradle
sources.bestFor: Forge workspace, mappings, runs, reobfuscation, and packaging
sources.notes: Required for many legacy Forge source recoveries and rebuilds.

sources.name: Forgified Fabric API
sources.bestFor: NeoForge implementation and adaptation of Fabric API modules
sources.notes: Core dependency for Connector-based compatibility.

sources.name: japicmp
sources.bestFor: Binary compatibility and API difference analysis for Java archives
sources.notes: Core evidence generator for missing methods, fields, classes, and descriptor changes.

sources.name: JDK javap, jdeps, jar, and jarsigner
sources.bestFor: Class descriptors, dependency analysis, archive integrity, signatures, and Java level
sources.notes: Always available in a correct JDK toolchain and essential for independent verification.

sources.name: mapping-io
sources.bestFor: Read, write, transform, and compare mapping formats
sources.notes: Core namespace graph library for legacy and cross-loader work.

sources.name: mcmeta
sources.bestFor: Generated vanilla reports, registries, tags, recipes, and version diffs
sources.notes: Excellent machine-readable source for assets and data-pack migration rules.

sources.name: Minecraft Java release notes
sources.bestFor: Authoritative game changes, pack versions, Java requirements, and release dates
sources.notes: Use exact release pages when building an adjacent-version migration chain.

sources.name: Minecraft Repair Brain
sources.bestFor: Versioned successful, partial, failed and superseded repair records with exact signatures, hashes, applicability, anti-patterns and runtime evidence
sources.notes: Canonical user-owned repair memory. Search before every repair and append only after evidence is preserved; never replace failed or superseded history with a cleaned-up success narrative.

sources.name: MinecraftForge
sources.bestFor: Forge loader and API implementation
sources.notes: Primary source for Forge symbols and loader behavior.

sources.name: ModDevGradle
sources.bestFor: Modern NeoForge mod development, runs, mappings, testing, and dependency setup
sources.notes: Preferred current NeoForge development path.

sources.name: ModForge
sources.bestFor: Deterministic source migration, cross-version symbol resolution, target-JAR verification, API deltas and Mixin target checks
sources.notes: Current high-capability leader for evidence-backed mapping migration. Its EXACT/CANDIDATE/UNRESOLVED model is suitable for guarded automation; observed release 0.1.2 on 2026-08-20.

sources.name: ModLens MCP
sources.bestFor: Persistent JAR ingestion, dependency graphs, class and Mixin indexes, decompilation, source search, bytecode diffs, crash facts and agent-accessible analysis
sources.notes: Strongest current external analysis/indexing candidate. Embedded SQLite is the zero-setup path; Vineflower and its bytecode indexer are acquired on demand. Inspect exact release and schema before enabling write actions.

sources.name: Modrinth API documentation
sources.bestFor: Project, version, dependency, hash, loader, and game-version resolution
sources.notes: Use SHA-512 identity and version metadata for exact update and dependency plans.

sources.name: Mojang version manifest v2
sources.bestFor: Machine-readable Java version and asset metadata
sources.notes: Use as the canonical version catalog and never infer latest versions from filenames.

sources.name: NeoForge
sources.bestFor: NeoForge loader and API implementation
sources.notes: Primary source for NeoForge symbols, behavior, tests, and migration verification.

sources.name: NeoForge Game Tests
sources.bestFor: Automated in-game structure and behavior tests
sources.notes: Core real-runtime verification layer for NeoForge repairs.

sources.name: NeoForge migration primers
sources.bestFor: Adjacent Minecraft and NeoForge API migrations
sources.notes: Best maintained public chain of vanilla and NeoForge migration notes, including 1.21.11 to 26.1 and 26.1.x to 26.2.

sources.name: ObjectWeb ASM
sources.bestFor: Authoritative low-level Java bytecode reading, analysis, verification, and transformation
sources.notes: Foundation for deterministic class repair and verification.

sources.name: OpenRewrite
sources.bestFor: Recipe-based Java source migration with parsers, type attribution, and repeatable rewrites
sources.notes: Best overall engine candidate for verified Minecraft API migration recipes.

sources.name: packwiz
sources.bestFor: Create, update, distribute, and export CurseForge and Modrinth packs
sources.notes: Best git-friendly pack metadata engine to integrate or interoperate with.

sources.name: Prism Launcher
sources.bestFor: Open-source multi-instance launcher with loaders, packs, logs, and Java management
sources.notes: Primary desktop instance integration target.

sources.name: Sinytra Connector
sources.bestFor: Runs many Fabric mods on NeoForge through remapping, patching, and API bridges
sources.notes: Best current high-capability Fabric to NeoForge runtime bridge. Treat compatibility as per-mod evidence, not universal proof.

sources.name: SpongePowered Mixin source
sources.bestFor: Exact annotation retention, injection semantics, refmaps, services, and bytecode weaving contracts
sources.notes: Inspect source and classfiles together when wiki guidance is insufficient; annotation processor and runtime contracts are both migration-critical.

sources.name: SpongePowered Mixin wiki
sources.bestFor: Mixin injection, selectors, refmaps, obfuscation, debugging, and compatibility
sources.notes: Primary reference for mixin target and injection repairs.

sources.name: Tiny Remapper
sources.bestFor: High-performance Java bytecode remapping
sources.notes: Primary Fabric ecosystem remapper and a strong foundation for Vault namespace transforms.

sources.name: Vineflower
sources.bestFor: Modern Java decompiler descended from FernFlower and Quiltflower
sources.notes: Best overall current decompiler candidate for source recovery pipelines.

sources.name: GitHub REST releases API
sources.bestFor: Release assets, tags, version lineage, checksums, and source/binary recovery
sources.notes: The current versioned API documents release asset SHA-256 digests and latest/tag endpoints; do not equate a tag with a published release.

sources.name: Gradle JVM toolchains
sources.bestFor: Reproducible JDK selection across Minecraft and loader generations
sources.notes: Current Gradle 9.7 documentation recommends toolchains and combining them with --release for strict bytecode/API compatibility.

sources.name: GitHub REST repository contents API
sources.bestFor: Resolving source trees, build files, tags, commits, and repository provenance
sources.notes: Use versioned REST requests and preserve commit SHA plus content digest for reproducible source recovery.

sources.name: Access Widener
sources.bestFor: Fabric access widening format and transformer
sources.notes: Required for correct Fabric source and binary reconstruction.

sources.name: Architectury Loom
sources.bestFor: Multi-loader mappings, remapping, platform builds, and run tasks
sources.notes: Strong foundation for common source across Fabric, Forge, NeoForge, and Quilt generations.

sources.name: Crash Assistant
sources.bestFor: Collecting launcher/game logs, crash reports and hs_err files, matching common causes, support routing and selected automatic fixes
sources.notes: Strong end-user crash intake companion. Import its proven signatures and remediation evidence, while retaining the Vault repair brain as the canonical deduplicated history.

sources.name: CurseForge for Studios API
sources.bestFor: Fingerprint matching, project files, dependencies, and game versions
sources.notes: Requires configured credentials for reliable automated resolution.

sources.name: Ferium
sources.bestFor: Fast CLI mod and modpack upgrades using Modrinth and CurseForge
sources.notes: Strong updater benchmark and potential provider-resolution adapter.

sources.name: MCPConfig
sources.bestFor: Forge mapping and patch configuration for Minecraft versions
sources.notes: Core legacy Forge namespace reconstruction source.

sources.name: MinecraftForge documentation
sources.bestFor: Forge concepts, registries, events, data generation, ForgeGradle, and migration notes
sources.notes: Coverage varies by Minecraft generation; inspect Forge source and MDKs when docs lag.

sources.name: Misode Minecraft version changelog
sources.bestFor: Data pack, resource pack, registry, command, and JSON format changes
sources.notes: Best paired with Mojang release notes and generated reports.

sources.name: MixinExtras
sources.bestFor: Safer and more expressive mixin injection primitives
sources.notes: Prefer recognized MixinExtras semantics over brittle custom redirects when source can be repaired.

sources.name: Modrinth App
sources.bestFor: Open-source launcher and Modrinth instance manager
sources.notes: Useful for profile format and update behavior comparisons.

sources.name: Recaf
sources.bestFor: Bytecode and resource inspection, editing, decompilation, and scripting
sources.notes: Excellent interactive repair workbench and potential headless analysis integration.

sources.name: spark
sources.bestFor: CPU, memory, tick, and heap profiling for Minecraft clients and servers
sources.notes: Required evidence source for performance repair without feature reduction.

sources.name: Stonecutter
sources.bestFor: Versioned source sets and conditional code across Minecraft versions
sources.notes: One of the strongest tools for maintaining many Minecraft versions from one repository.

sources.name: Sinytra Probe
sources.bestFor: Offline Connector transformation checks and large-scale Fabric-on-NeoForge compatibility triage
sources.notes: Probe 0.1.64 powered the July 2026 Connector 3.0.0-beta.1 compatibility run. Its maintainers explicitly warn that successful patching does not prove in-game behavior.

sources.name: Spyglass
sources.bestFor: Language-server parsing, validation, completion and schema intelligence for Minecraft data packs, resource packs and mcdoc schemas
sources.notes: Best current structured-text validation candidate for resource/data migration. Use exact target-version schemas and treat semantic world behavior as a separate runtime test.

sources.name: Amulet Map Editor and Core
sources.bestFor: Java and Bedrock world editing and format translation
sources.notes: Strong base for world-level repair and conversion on copied saves.

sources.name: Architectury documentation
sources.bestFor: Cross-loader project structure, common code, Architectury Loom, and platform APIs
sources.notes: Useful for source-level loader convergence, not a magic binary converter.

sources.name: Architectury Plugin
sources.bestFor: Platform transformation and common-module injection for Architectury projects
sources.notes: Pair with Architectury Loom when reconstructing a unified multi-loader source tree.

sources.name: Auto Renaming Tool
sources.bestFor: Forge-oriented JAR renaming and mapping application
sources.notes: Use for SRG and official mapping transformations where applicable.

sources.name: CFR
sources.bestFor: Independent Java decompiler with excellent language feature coverage
sources.notes: Use as a second decompiler to cross-check ambiguous Vineflower output.

sources.name: Enigma
sources.bestFor: Interactive deobfuscation, mapping editing, analysis, and statistics
sources.notes: Still valuable for legacy versions and undocumented third-party binaries.

sources.name: GumTree
sources.bestFor: AST-aware source differencing and edit scripts
sources.notes: Use to mine upstream mod ports and loader API changes into candidate rewrite rules.

sources.name: HeadlessMC
sources.bestFor: Headless Minecraft launch and automation
sources.notes: High-value isolated client/server smoke-test runner.

sources.name: JavaParser
sources.bestFor: Java AST parsing, symbol solving, editing, and code generation
sources.notes: Good for focused transformations where full OpenRewrite recipes are unnecessary.

sources.name: JUnit 5
sources.bestFor: Unit and integration test framework
sources.notes: Use for generated migration recipes, parsers, and deterministic patch tests.

sources.name: mc-publish
sources.bestFor: Publishes mod artifacts to multiple Minecraft platforms from CI
sources.notes: Useful for reconstructed mod release pipelines and proof artifacts.

sources.name: MCMan
sources.bestFor: Declarative Minecraft server and modpack management
sources.notes: Useful server-side pack definition and reproducibility benchmark.

sources.name: Minecraft Development IntelliJ Plugin
sources.bestFor: IDE support for loaders, mappings, mixins, access transformers, and run configs
sources.notes: Useful in generated source projects and manual repair review.

sources.name: MixinTrace
sources.bestFor: Adds mixin attribution to stack traces
sources.notes: High-value crash diagnosis input for automatic root-cause ranking.

sources.name: packwiz documentation
sources.bestFor: Git-friendly pack metadata, updates, side declarations, exports, and installer flows
sources.notes: Useful as an interchange and regression fixture format.

sources.name: ParchmentMC documentation
sources.bestFor: Parameter names and Javadocs layered on official mappings
sources.notes: Particularly valuable after 26.1 because documentation remains useful even when obfuscation ends.

sources.name: Prism Launcher wiki
sources.bestFor: Instance layout, mod management, logs, Java, loaders, and pack import/export
sources.notes: Excellent real-instance integration target for Vault repair workflows.

sources.name: PrismarineJS minecraft-data
sources.bestFor: Machine-readable protocol, blocks, items, entities, recipes, and version data
sources.notes: Strong cross-version structured data source, especially outside loader APIs.

sources.name: Renovate
sources.bestFor: Automated Gradle, GitHub Actions, Java, and custom dependency updates
sources.notes: Strong foundation for continuous loader, mappings, and library update PRs.

sources.name: Retromod
sources.bestFor: AOT and runtime transformation of older mod bytecode, mappings, Mixins, access rules, metadata and nested JARs for newer Minecraft hosts
sources.notes: Highest-ambition binary compatibility project found. Treat its compatibility database and exact tuple tests as mandatory gates; complex renderer, loader and save-affecting mods still need source ports or targeted adapters.

sources.name: Revapi
sources.bestFor: Extensible API analysis and compatibility checking
sources.notes: Use alongside japicmp for richer API policy and extension points.

sources.name: Spoon
sources.bestFor: Typed Java metamodel, analysis, transformations, and pretty printing
sources.notes: Strong alternative for semantic source repairs and mining migration patterns.

sources.name: MC Mod Porter
sources.bestFor: Adjacent-version source migrations, build metadata updates, known API rewrite rules, resource migrations and build-error reporting from Minecraft 1.16 through current calendar versions
sources.notes: Useful rule corpus and source-workspace automation. Use only against extracted source projects; logic redesigns and third-party API changes still require evidence-backed engineering. Observed beta 1.1.3.

sources.name: Modstitch
sources.bestFor: One build DSL over Fabric Loom and NeoForge ModDevGradle, metadata generation, Mixin registration and access-widener/access-transformer transpilation
sources.notes: High-capability unified build layer, currently published through unstable plugin versions. Pin exact plugin/toolchain tuples and run every target build before adopting generated changes.

sources.name: Unimined
sources.bestFor: One Gradle extension spanning modern and legacy Minecraft, multiple loaders, mappings, remapping, runs and custom transformation pipelines
sources.notes: Broadest build-tool reach in the catalog, especially valuable for legacy recovery. Use the current LTS branch and validate exact loader/version support instead of assuming every matrix cell is complete.

sources.name: ATLauncher
sources.bestFor: Open-source launcher and pack manager
sources.notes: Important additional instance format and provider workflow.

sources.name: ClassGraph
sources.bestFor: Fast classpath, annotation, dependency, and resource scanning
sources.notes: Candidate for deep dependency graph and side-only class analysis.

sources.name: CodeQL
sources.bestFor: Deep semantic code queries and data flow analysis
sources.notes: Use for high-risk native, reflection, network, serialization, and injection analysis.

sources.name: Geyser
sources.bestFor: Bedrock to Java protocol translation
sources.notes: Useful for Bedrock compatibility test matrices and server integration.

sources.name: Jared's MultiLoader Template
sources.bestFor: Reference structure for common, Fabric, Forge, and NeoForge modules
sources.notes: Use as a comparison target, not blindly as a replacement for project-specific build logic.

sources.name: mclo.gs
sources.bestFor: Log parsing, syntax highlighting, sharing, and analysis API
sources.notes: Use as an optional log normalization and sharing adapter.

sources.name: Minecraft Wiki
sources.bestFor: Game mechanics, technical formats, commands, NBT, data packs, and historical changes
sources.notes: Strong secondary technical reference; confirm loader-specific claims in loader docs.

sources.name: Minotaur
sources.bestFor: Official Modrinth Gradle publishing plugin
sources.notes: Use when rebuilding source projects that publish to Modrinth.

sources.name: Quilt Loader
sources.bestFor: Quilt loading, metadata, dependency solving, and Fabric compatibility
sources.notes: Treat Quilt Loader as active while QSL and new Quilt Mappings are retired.

sources.name: Semgrep
sources.bestFor: Pattern and semantic static analysis across source trees
sources.notes: Useful for migration anti-pattern rules and security scanning.

sources.name: StackDeobfuscator
sources.bestFor: Maps obfuscated stack traces at runtime
sources.notes: Useful for older mapped environments and crash ingestion.

sources.name: ViaVersion
sources.bestFor: Minecraft protocol translation across versions
sources.notes: Useful for protocol compatibility analysis, not mod API conversion.

sources.name: Balm
sources.bestFor: Battle-tested common APIs and events for Fabric, Forge and NeoForge source projects without custom Gradle magic
sources.notes: Strong reference architecture for loader abstraction and third-party integrations. It is a source library, not a binary cross-loader converter.

sources.name: Cloche
sources.bestFor: Target-oriented multi-version and multi-loader Minecraft builds, generated metadata, data generation, tests, runs and source-set separation
sources.notes: Promising high-capability alternative architecture. Its pre-applied Mixin/debug paths include work-in-progress areas, so adopt behind generated-workspace tests.

sources.name: NBT Studio
sources.bestFor: Interactive Java, Bedrock, SNBT and region-file inspection and editing with undo/redo and format conversion
sources.notes: Modern manual verification companion to NBTExplorer. Keep automated repairs deterministic and use NBT Studio for human inspection of copied saves and structures.

sources.name: BinaryPatcher
sources.bestFor: Forge binary patch creation and application
sources.notes: Useful for deterministic distribution of narrow binary deltas.

sources.name: Brigadier
sources.bestFor: Minecraft command parsing and syntax trees
sources.notes: Useful for command migration and validation.

sources.name: Connector Extras
sources.bestFor: Additional compatibility patches for Fabric mods running through Connector
sources.notes: Use only when exact mod evidence supports the patch set.

sources.name: CurseGradle
sources.bestFor: Gradle publishing integration for CurseForge
sources.notes: Use for compatible legacy and current CurseForge publication workflows.

sources.name: DiffPatch
sources.bestFor: Source and archive patch generation and application
sources.notes: Candidate for reproducible migration patch bundles.

sources.name: Error Prone and Refaster
sources.bestFor: Compile-time bug checks and template-based Java rewrites
sources.notes: Refaster can encode compact API replacement templates after rules are verified.

sources.name: Fabric Language Kotlin
sources.bestFor: Kotlin runtime and adapter for Fabric mods
sources.notes: Detect Kotlin metadata before source migration or bytecode rewriting.

sources.name: GDLauncher Carbon
sources.bestFor: Modern open-source Minecraft launcher
sources.notes: Useful for multi-launcher import and update compatibility.

sources.name: Gradle Versions Plugin
sources.bestFor: Reports dependency and plugin updates
sources.notes: Use as an inventory source, not as the final compatibility decision.

sources.name: JarSplitter
sources.bestFor: Splits classes and resources for modern toolchain pipelines
sources.notes: Useful in NeoForge and mapping preparation workflows.

sources.name: Lorenz
sources.bestFor: Mapping model and transformations
sources.notes: Useful for format-independent mapping operations.

sources.name: MCA Selector
sources.bestFor: Region inspection, selection, filtering, and deletion
sources.notes: Useful for targeted region recovery and reproducible world test fixtures.

sources.name: Porting Lib
sources.bestFor: Forge-like abstractions and porting helpers on Fabric
sources.notes: Useful for source ports that depend on Forge concepts, especially Create-derived ecosystems.

sources.name: Querz NBT
sources.bestFor: Java NBT and region file library
sources.notes: Candidate for direct world and structure repair modules.

sources.name: QuiltMC documentation and status
sources.bestFor: Quilt Loader, Enigma, configuration, and current project status
sources.notes: Quilt Mappings and QSL are retired for new versions; retain for legacy repair only.

sources.name: SpecialSource
sources.bestFor: Class, member, and inheritance-aware remapping
sources.notes: Useful for Bukkit, Forge, and older mapping pipelines.

sources.name: Stonecraft
sources.bestFor: Reducing multi-version, multi-loader Gradle duplication around Stonecutter and Architectury with a versioned plugin and template
sources.notes: Good productivity layer for source-owned projects already aligned with Architectury. Validate generated configuration and publishing tasks for every supported tuple.

sources.name: ViaFabricPlus
sources.bestFor: Fabric client protocol translation and old-version behavior compatibility
sources.notes: Useful for cross-version connection testing, not a substitute for porting mods.

sources.name: Burger
sources.bestFor: Extracts structured information from Minecraft jars
sources.notes: Useful for historical metadata extraction and cross-checking generated catalogs.

sources.name: Chunker
sources.bestFor: Java and Bedrock world conversion
sources.notes: Treat as an external conversion lane and verify exact output versions.

sources.name: Kilt
sources.bestFor: Forge mod compatibility on Fabric
sources.notes: High-value opposite-direction bridge, but verify supported Minecraft and Forge API coverage per build.

sources.name: Mercury
sources.bestFor: Java source transformation and remapping
sources.notes: Candidate for source-level namespace conversions after decompilation.

sources.name: NeoGradle
sources.bestFor: NeoForge Gradle tooling for projects still using its model
sources.notes: Keep for existing project migration; prefer ModDevGradle for new reconstructed projects when supported.

sources.name: Not Enough Crashes
sources.bestFor: Improved crash handling and reports in Fabric environments
sources.notes: Useful supplemental client diagnostics where supported.

sources.name: Observable
sources.bestFor: In-game tick-time profiling and visualization
sources.notes: Useful for entity and block-entity hot spot diagnosis.

sources.name: Testcontainers for Java
sources.bestFor: Disposable containerized integration environments
sources.notes: Useful for server management and provider-adapter tests, though not a substitute for real Minecraft runtime tests.

sources.name: Hopper
sources.bestFor: Runtime resolution and loading of server-plugin dependencies from Hangar, Modrinth, Spiget, GitHub Releases and direct URLs with platform/version policies
sources.notes: Useful design source for the server-plugin lane. Hot-loading and third-party dependency resolution require isolated runtime and rollback tests before integration.

sources.name: Multisource
sources.bestFor: Source-set and Gradle feature-variant modeling of Fabric and NeoForge targets with delegated Loom projects
sources.notes: Interesting low-duplication multiloader architecture, but smaller and less proven than Architectury, Stonecutter or Modstitch. Evaluate through a generated sacrificial workspace first.

sources.name: NBTExplorer
sources.bestFor: Interactive NBT inspection and editing
sources.notes: Useful manual verification tool for save and config repairs.

sources.name: Quilt Loom
sources.bestFor: Quilt workspace and mappings tooling for supported legacy and current projects
sources.notes: Evaluate project version before choosing over Fabric Loom.

sources.name: MixinSquared
sources.bestFor: Mixins targeting other mixins for compatibility patches
sources.notes: Powerful last-resort compatibility mechanism; keep scope narrow and test exact competing transforms.

sources.name: Blahaj
sources.bestFor: Automated Stonecutter-based multiversion project management, dependencies, compatibility declarations and publishing configuration
sources.notes: Bleeding-edge candidate with limited adoption evidence. Mine ideas and benchmark against Stonecraft/Stonecutter before any direct dependency decision.

sources.name: Srg2Source
sources.bestFor: Legacy Forge source range and mapping transformations
sources.notes: Keep for older Forge recovery only.

sources.name: ReForged
sources.bestFor: NeoForge mod compatibility on Forge 1.21.1 through bytecode transforms and shims
sources.notes: Bleeding-edge research candidate. Restrictive licensing and narrow target mean no code transplant into Vault.

sources.name: Insanity Wrapper
sources.bestFor: Fabric and Quilt compatibility layer on NeoForge for newer versions
sources.notes: Research candidate with restrictive license and manual mapping workflow.

sources.name: Modrinth Pack Version Updater
sources.bestFor: Checks a Modrinth pack against another Minecraft version
sources.notes: Use as a test corpus and UX reference, not the core solver.

sources.name: ModMorpher
sources.bestFor: Compiled-JAR decompile and conversion experiments
sources.notes: Useful for ideas and test cases, not a trusted production converter.

sources.name: Patchwork Patcher
sources.bestFor: Historical Fabric to Forge binary patching research
sources.notes: Do not adopt as a current engine; mine architecture and failure lessons only.

sources.name: NeoForm
sources.bestFor: Reproducible, recompilable modern Minecraft source reconstruction and adjacent-version patch updates
sources.notes: Use createPatchWorkspace/createPatchWorkspaceForUpdate and preserve branch/tag provenance. Obfuscated and unobfuscated Minecraft generations use different NeoForm branches.

sources.name: NeoForm Runtime
sources.bestFor: Standalone execution graphs that deobfuscate, merge, patch, recompile, and emit exact Minecraft or NeoForge artifacts
sources.notes: High-value deterministic backend for isolated source recovery. Pin NeoForm/NeoForge coordinates and capture the printed execution graph and every output hash.

sources.name: RetroMCP-Java
sources.bestFor: Recovering, remapping, editing, recompiling, and reobfuscating many alpha, beta, and legacy release workspaces
sources.notes: Use for versions outside modern NeoForm/MCPConfig coverage. Preserve the selected version profile, mappings, patches, decompiler, and reobfuscation output.

sources.name: RetroFuturaGradle
sources.bestFor: Modern, cache-aware Minecraft 1.7.10 Forge source builds and reliable reobfuscation
sources.notes: Current 2.x line supports Gradle 9 and requires Java 25 for the build process. Runtime target compatibility remains a separate test.

sources.name: RetroFuturaBootstrap
sources.bestFor: Backwards-compatible LaunchWrapper replacement, transformer diagnostics, and early compatibility plugins on modern Java
sources.notes: Use class-dump and per-transformer evidence to diagnose legacy bootstrap failures. It is a runtime foundation, not a source port by itself.

sources.name: Cleanroom
sources.bestFor: Running and developing Minecraft 1.12.2 on modern Java and LWJGL3 with loader and mod compatibility patches
sources.notes: Treat broad compatibility claims as hypotheses until the exact pack and feature set passes client, server, restart, world, rendering, and transformer tests.

sources.name: MixinBooter
sources.bestFor: Unified Mixin bootstrap and diagnostics for Minecraft 1.8 through 1.12.2
sources.notes: Use the current CleanMix-backed line, register configs explicitly, and retain dedicated mixin logs and class-loading traces.

sources.name: UniMixins
sources.bestFor: Modular, compatibility-oriented Mixin loading for 1.7.10 with partial 1.8.9 through 1.12.2 support
sources.notes: 0.3.1 is the current verified release as of 2026-08-20. Choose modules deliberately and reject overlapping Mixin providers.

sources.name: LWJGL3ify
sources.bestFor: Running Minecraft 1.7.10 with LWJGL3 and modern Java while exposing concrete compatibility patch requirements
sources.notes: Depends on UniMixins and bundles RetroFuturaBootstrap. Validate graphics, natives, coremods, reflection, server startup, and pack-specific fixes independently.

sources.name: Fugue
sources.bestFor: Targeted compatibility patches that keep selected 1.12.2 mods functioning under Cleanroom and modern Java
sources.notes: Use as an explicit per-mod patch candidate, not a blanket proof that a pack is compatible. Preserve patch ownership and exact tested versions.

sources.name: PaperMC DataConverter
sources.bestFor: Studying high-performance, debuggable vanilla data conversion and schema-walker alternatives to DFU
sources.notes: Never run its Fabric mod against modded worlds: it intentionally does not execute data fixers registered by other mods. Use only as architecture and test-corpus evidence unless targeting Paper/vanilla data.

sources.name: Mod Publish Plugin
sources.bestFor: Configuration-cache-compatible Gradle publishing to common Minecraft artifact destinations
sources.notes: Version 2.1.1 was current on 2026-08-20. Keep publication separate from build verification and verify remote bytes after upload.

sources.name: Forgix
sources.bestFor: Merging loader-specific Fabric, Quilt, Forge, and related outputs into one distributable JAR
sources.notes: 1.3.4 is the latest stable registry release; 2.0 exists as snapshots. Always retain and test each native loader artifact before trusting a merged JAR.

sources.name: ModShade
sources.bestFor: Relocating and shading plain Java libraries into a mod without polluting published dependency metadata
sources.notes: Do not use it to embed Fabric, Forge, NeoForge, or other Minecraft mod JARs; use loader-native nested-JAR metadata or declared mod dependencies.

sources.name: NeoForge Mod Generator
sources.bestFor: Generating clean current NeoForge target workspaces through the official web or CLI-capable generator core
sources.notes: Generate into a new branch/workspace and diff every produced setting before migrating source. The browser generator and CLI consume the same core.

sources.name: MCP-Reborn
sources.bestFor: Minecraft 1.13 through current-generation source reconstruction and code research
sources.notes: The project explicitly warns that generated code cannot be published. Use it for research, symbol comparison, and test workspaces, not as release-source output.

sources.name: Fabric Meta
sources.bestFor: Exact Fabric game, loader, intermediary, Yarn, installer, and launcher metadata resolution
sources.notes: Use the newest-first V2 endpoints, retain the stable flag and Maven coordinates, and cache with timestamped provenance.

sources.name: Ornithe Feather
sources.bestFor: Open legacy Minecraft mappings from c0.0.12a_03 through 1.14.4 and mapped/decompiled comparison workspaces
sources.notes: Use with Ploceus/Loom, preserve version graph provenance, and mark generated decompiler output as research unless independently rebuilt and reviewed.

sources.name: Ornithe Ploceus
sources.bestFor: Extending Fabric/Quilt Loom for Ornithe legacy mappings, loaders, runs, and builds
sources.notes: Prefer the official Ornithe template and pin mappings, loader, Loom/Ploceus, Java, and target version as one tested tuple.

sources.name: Legacy Fabric API
sources.bestFor: Fabric hooks and interoperability modules for Minecraft 1.3.x through 1.13.2
sources.notes: Use the repository's per-version module support matrix; do not assume every API module exists or behaves identically on every legacy release.

sources.name: Legacy Looming
sources.bestFor: Extending Fabric Loom for Legacy Fabric Minecraft versions
sources.notes: Pin it together with Legacy Intermediaries, Legacy Yarn/API, loader, Gradle, and Java. Verify remap and run tasks on the exact old version.

sources.name: StationAPI
sources.bestFor: General-purpose Babric/Fabric API development on Minecraft Beta 1.7.3
sources.notes: Use its official example/template path and test with the recommended Java/runtime tuple. It is an API ecosystem, not a generic converter.

sources.name: LegacyFix
sources.bestFor: Runtime and coremod patches across legacy vanilla, Forge, and Fabric installations
sources.notes: Install mode changes by Minecraft version and loader. Test it as a distinct compatibility layer and keep the unpatched baseline.

sources.name: Ornithe Gitcraft
sources.bestFor: Generating decompiled Minecraft version-history repositories and exact adjacent-version source diffs
sources.notes: Generated repositories must not be shared. Use identity, Mojmap, Yarn, Feather, or Calamus mappings to isolate API and implementation changes.

sources.name: FPGradle
sources.bestFor: Declarative Minecraft 1.7.10 Forge development and modernized legacy project configuration
sources.notes: 2.1.1 was the current verified plugin release. Compare against RetroFuturaGradle on the exact source project instead of assuming one build layer fits all.

sources.name: Hodgepodge
sources.bestFor: Pack-level bug, performance, and modern-Java compatibility patches for Minecraft 1.7.10
sources.notes: LWJGL3ify explicitly recommends it for Java 17+ compatibility gaps in several older mods. Enable only relevant fixes and verify pack behavior.

sources.name: InterMed
sources.bestFor: Read-only, source-traceable analysis of mods, packs, servers, logs, Mixins, resources, security and performance evidence
sources.notes: Use JSON/SARIF/HTML findings as evidence inside isolated workspaces. Version 0.1.4-alpha was reviewed on 2026-08-20; output contracts may change and no finding is an automatic repair.

sources.name: modcrawl
sources.bestFor: Fast loader, metadata, dependency, class, constant-pool, Mixin and duplicate-class inspection
sources.notes: Young Rust CLI/library/FFI project. Pin exact revisions and compare JSON output against Vault fixtures before relying on it.

sources.name: Modpack Inspector
sources.bestFor: Desktop pack inventory, dependency graphs, provider enrichment, config ownership clues and log-oriented inspection
sources.notes: Useful human-facing second opinion; never auto-delete libraries or configs from heuristic findings.

sources.name: ModpackResolver
sources.bestFor: Coarse identification of Minecraft versions with the broadest selected-mod availability
sources.notes: Availability is not loader/API/runtime compatibility. Re-resolve exact files, dependencies and behavior before acting.
